title: 6.24.2 Sub-build: A square that does something
description: Six squares, two letters, one token. After each step, the letter under the token decides what happens.

steps.title: Run it
steps.instructions: SPACE steps the token one square at a time, and the J and the S do nothing.

steps.title: Jump on a J
steps.instructions: After `at += 1`, read the letter under the token: `ROW[at]`. If it is `'J'`, move ahead 2 with `at = min(at + 2, ROW.length - 1)` and set `note` to say so. From square 0, one SPACE should land on the J and carry on to square 3.
hints: `ROW[at]` is the letter the token is standing on, like `path[p.at].kind` in the reading.

steps.title: Slide on an S
steps.instructions: If the letter is `'S'`, send the token back to the start: `at = 0`. Step onto square 4 and watch it go back.
hints: `else if` makes it clear that only one letter can match.

requirements.title: Reads the letter under the token
requirements.description: The code reads the letter at the token's square. Help: 6.24.1 (Reading: The square decides)

requirements.title: J moves ahead
requirements.description: Landing on a J moves the token forward. Help: 6.24.1 (Reading: The square decides)

requirements.title: S moves back
requirements.description: Landing on an S moves the token back. Help: 6.24.1 (Reading: The square decides)

aiCheck.rubricTitle: What the AI read in your code
aiCheck.prompt: The student wrote a moSHion sketch for "Sub-build: A square that does something". The task: after each step, read the letter of the square under the token; on J move ahead 2 (staying on the row), on S go back to the start. Accept any names, helpers, ternaries and semicolons; a line only in a comment or string does not count. Short, plain notes for a 14-year-old; never write corrected code.

rubric.title: Reads the square
rubric.description: The letter at the token is checked after the step.
